_note: Ordinary people with a concrete moment, never famous or senior-expert personas (Deng 2026: ordinary 57.0 vs creative-celebrity 50.4 unique combinations; Chen 2026: expertise plus authority collapses diversity). 'role' = a relation to this project; 'outsider' = an ordinary person dropped into it. roll.mjs alternates the pools.

role.line: someone installing this for the first time
role.moment: they followed the README and the first command did something they did not expect

role.line: the author, back after nine months away
role.moment: they forgot how this works and need to change one thing today

role.line: a contributor who forked this and only reads error messages
role.moment: something failed and the message is all they have

role.line: the person who uses this every day
role.moment: the tenth time today they do the same steps

role.line: the person on call who did not write this
role.moment: it broke at 3am and they must explain what happened

role.line: a reviewer reading a pull request against this code
role.moment: they must decide in five minutes whether a change is safe

role.line: someone wiring this into another tool or script
role.moment: they need its output in a shape a machine can read

role.line: someone demoing this live to a room
role.moment: they have thirty seconds to show why it is good

outsider.line: a nurse who became a developer last month
outsider.moment: day one at a new job, told to 'just run it'

outsider.line: a support person who answers user complaints
outsider.moment: they must explain a failure to a customer in one sentence

outsider.line: a teacher showing this to thirty students
outsider.moment: half the class is stuck on the same step

outsider.line: someone on an old laptop and a slow hotel network
outsider.moment: every step that waits feels twice as long

outsider.line: a user who works in another language and time zone
outsider.moment: dates, words and defaults all assume someone else

outsider.line: an auditor asking who changed what and why
outsider.moment: they need a trail and there is none

outsider.line: a manager who reads only release notes
outsider.moment: deciding whether this is worth a team's week

outsider.line: a small shop owner who hires one developer
outsider.moment: they pay per hour and want fewer surprises

outsider.line: a retired bus driver learning to code as a hobby
outsider.moment: they read every word and take every instruction literally

outsider.line: a first-year student copying this for a project
outsider.moment: they will copy whatever the README shows, mistakes included
